taxonomy.note: Accepted species verified with Kew/POWO and ITIS.

evidence: Hays — UT Austin Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve, N. Hays County explicitly records Bouteloua rigidiseta.
Travis — Fowler (2002) documents Bouteloua rigidiseta as abundant in flat plots at Shield Ranch in western Travis County.
Williamson — UT Austin Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment of Bouteloua rigidiseta.
target_zone_range.guardrail: BONAP/NPSOT county mapping supports the broader native pattern; county names above come from explicit local/county records rather than inference.

morphology.look_here_first: Count and inspect the short inflorescence branches near the top: Texas grama usually has about 5–9 tiny, densely hairy/awned lateral branches, often secondarily arranged to one side, instead of the many hanging racemes of sideoats or the 1–3 long combs of blue grama.
diagnostic_traits: small perennial bunchgrass, often under about 50 cm
leaves narrow, often wavy or curled, crowded toward the base but also cauline
terminal racemelike panicle with roughly 5–9 short condensed lateral branches
branches short and densely pubescent with conspicuous awns
clusters of several spikelets with woolly bases
smooth dark nodes on slender weak culms

confusers.separator: Sideoats grama carries many more short racemes spaced down an elongated axis; Texas grama has only several tiny fuzzy/awned branches clustered much nearer the top.
Blue grama normally has 1–3 longer curved pectinate 'eyebrow' racemes; Texas grama has several much shorter fuzzy/awned branches, usually around 5–9.
